definition: A very large neural network, typically a Transformer, trained on massive text to predict and generate language.
details: LLMs learn statistical patterns of language and code from enormous corpora, and at scale display abilities such as instruction following, reasoning and tool use. A survey of the field maps their architecture, training, adaptation and evaluation, and describes the tuning, alignment and prompting techniques that turn a text predictor into an assistant.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. And that is Large Language Model — teaching a machine to read between the lines.

citation.title: A Survey of Large Language Models
